description: Implementation obligations derived from committed goals: each entry carries the contract, a concise implementation summary, its gate tests, and known limits.

requirements.title: Sidecar identity for the hash short-circuit
requirements.statement: If the hash short-circuit is enabled, the submit snapshot or the stored row carries sidecar identity, so deleting or changing a sidecar changes the identity and forces reprocessing rather than a skip.
requirements.gate: Backend test with the hash short-circuit enabled: index an asset whose sidecar was present, delete the sidecar, resubmit/scan; the row's sidecar identity changes and sidecar-derived state is cleared.
requirements.implementation: Deferred with the hash short-circuit. Rescans currently reprocess and clear sidecar-derived state; the identity is required only when the skip is re-enabled.
requirements.limits: IntakeItem carries mtime/len only; AssetRecord has no sidecar field.

requirements.title: File rename submits old-path remove plus new-path create
requirements.statement: A rename delivered by the watcher submits a remove for the old path and an index for the new path, so the row follows without waiting for a sweep.
requirements.gate: Backend test: rename a watched file; the row disappears at the old path and appears at the new one without a sweep.
requirements.implementation: Watcher `Name(Both/From/To)` events submit old-path removal and new-path indexing before the generic modify arm; `Any/Other` keeps generic indexing.
requirements.limits: A split `From`/`To` pair without a destination is left to the sweep/backstop.

requirements.title: Directory rename follows descendants atomically
requirements.statement: A watched directory rename updates every contained asset's row to the renamed path in one step, preserving assetId and sidecar association, with no ghosts and no re-decode.
requirements.gate: Backend test: rename a watched directory; every descendant row follows to the new path with assetId preserved.
requirements.implementation: A directory rename is detected when the new path is a directory; watcher and API album moves lease the old and new subtrees and bump those paths while descendant rows are rewritten in place (assetId and sidecar association preserved) and the view epoch advances, without decoding. A dir-album verify re-resolves the album id to its current directory before pruning.
requirements.limits: Only `RenameMode::Both` carries the old path; split From/To falls back to sweep/backstop. The filesystem move happens before the row rewrite, so a crash between them needs a rescan.

requirements.title: Per-root sweep isolation is verified
requirements.statement: A scan of one root reaps only rows under that root; rows outside the scanned root survive even when their files are absent.
requirements.gate: Backend test: scan one sub-root with a ghost row outside it; the outside row survives the sweep.
requirements.implementation: Sweep already filters rows by `starts_with(root)`; added the isolation gate test.

requirements.title: Rescan on the watcher's Flag::Rescan signal
requirements.statement: An inotify overflow or rescan flag triggers a full rescan of the affected root instead of being ignored.
requirements.gate: Backend test with a forced overflow or synthetic Flag::Rescan event: the affected root is rescanned.
requirements.implementation: Watcher checks `Event::need_rescan()` before dispatch and submits a full scan of the image, users, or both roots based on event paths; a running job is a debug skip.

requirements.title: Configurable per-root periodic backstop scan
requirements.statement: The server can run a per-root full scan on a configurable interval; when enabled, a change missed by the watcher converges within one backstop cycle.
requirements.owner: scheduler, lifecycle and config (model/config.rs, lib.rs startup, tasks/lifecycle.rs)
requirements.gate: Integration test: with the backstop enabled and the watcher disabled, a missed change converges within one backstop interval; config test covers interval and root scope.
requirements.implementation: New `index_backstop_interval_secs` (gallery, default 0, env override). A lifecycle-owned backstop starts a scan job and awaits that job's completion on each interval; shutdown aborts the loop, rejects intake, cancels and awaits the active scan, then drains the writer.
requirements.limits: One loop scans both roots (`auto`); separate per-root loops are out of scope. Shutdown waits up to 10s for an in-flight scan before draining the writer.

requirements.title: Scans coordinate with in-flight mutating API work
requirements.statement: A scan or sweep running concurrently with an in-flight assign (or other multi-file mutation) neither prunes the moved row nor separates the asset from its sidecar; coordination is by exclusion or in-flight detection.
requirements.owner: album index, queue and mutating API (tasks/actor/album_index.rs, tasks/path_epoch.rs, tasks/queue, router/put/assign_album.rs, router/delete.rs)
requirements.gate: Concurrency test: an assign overlapping a scan/sweep keeps the moved row and its sidecar intact.
requirements.implementation: Per-path generations plus short exact/subtree leases replace the process-wide gate. Assign/delete/directory moves lease the paths or subtrees they mutate; delete holds its leases across the row flush. The sweep enqueues a Verify-lane item per stale record; the worker re-checks the path generation, any active lease, and the filesystem before the serial writer prunes. Thumbnail deletion happens in the confirmed writer removal, not in the sweep. Scan and watcher indexing skip a path under a lease.
requirements.limits: Leases are in-process and best-effort; no cross-process coordination. A verify that wins before a mutation acquires its lease relies on the serial writer re-resolving the record by path. A full lazy view rebuild remains a request-thread cost on very large libraries (scoped views are an open optimisation).

requirements.title: Per-row thumbnail checksum with scan regeneration
requirements.statement: Rows carry a thumbnail checksum; a scan regenerates the artifact when the bytes do not match, and a missing artifact still forces reprocessing.
requirements.gate: Backend test: corrupt a thumbnail's bytes; the next scan detects the mismatch and regenerates it.
requirements.implementation: Deferred with the hash short-circuit. Full rescans regenerate thumbnails, but no row checksum exists and corrupt bytes are not detected.
requirements.limits: Needs a skip consumer; returns with REQ-1.

requirements.title: Orphan .xmp detection is logged only
requirements.statement: A restart or scan reports sidecars without a media file in the log and never deletes them; the detection must not act concurrently with an in-flight mutation.
requirements.gate: Backend test: leave an .xmp with no media; scan/restart logs it and does not delete it.
requirements.implementation: The scan walk collects only `.xmp` paths; after drain/sweep it warns for sidecars whose directory holds no file with the same stem and a supported media extension. Sibling media is checked on demand, so the walk holds no per-media path list. Log only, never deletes.
requirements.limits: On-demand sibling checks cost one directory read per sidecar; false positives are log noise only.

requirements.title: Stale upload temp files are swept
requirements.statement: Upload crash residue (.upload-{filename}.{pid}.{seq}.tmp) is removed at startup or scan and is never indexed.
requirements.gate: Backend test: leave a tmp file; startup/scan removes it and no row is created for it.
requirements.implementation: Uploads stage as `.upload-{filename}.{pid}.{seq}.tmp`; startup walks image/users roots and removes owned temp names (`.upload-*`, `.sidecar-*`) whose pid is dead or whose mtime is older than an hour. Scans reject `.tmp` by extension.
requirements.limits: Startup-only by design; a long-running server keeps residue until restart. A live pid with a fresh mtime is kept, so a still-running abandoned temp survives that run.

requirements.title: Rotate writes the sidecar before the thumbnail and DB
requirements.statement: A rotate writes the sidecar rotation first, then the thumbnail, then the DB records, so any interruption leaves a present sidecar that forces reprocess.
requirements.gate: Backend test: fail the sidecar write and assert thumbnail and DB are unchanged; crash after the sidecar write and assert a rescan restores the rotation.
requirements.implementation: The route loads/applies rotation read-only, writes the sidecar rotation, then regenerates the thumbnail/metadata and flushes the DB; a sidecar failure leaves thumbnail and rows unchanged.

requirements.title: Assign copies the sidecar before moving the asset
requirements.statement: A multi-file assign copies the destination sidecar first, moves the asset, then removes the old sidecar; an interruption leaves at most an orphan copy, never an asset without its metadata.
requirements.gate: Backend test: interrupt after the sidecar copy and before the asset move; metadata is not separated.
requirements.implementation: Assign reads the source sidecar and writes it atomically beside the destination before moving the asset; the old sidecar is removed afterwards, best effort. A failed copy aborts; a failed move leaves only an orphan copy.
requirements.limits: DB updates remain after the move; they are not part of the sidecar-first guarantee.

requirements.title: Sidecar and albuminfo writes are atomic under partial-write failure
requirements.statement: A sidecar or albuminfo write either replaces the target completely or leaves the previous bytes untouched; no partial content is ever visible.
requirements.owner: sidecar edit and xmp write (process/sidecar_edit.rs, process/xmp_write.rs)
requirements.gate: Backend test: inject a failure inside the atomic helper after the temp file is partially written; the target keeps its previous bytes.
requirements.implementation: Both sidecar writers delegate to `write_via_temp`, which stages through `tempfile::NamedTempFile::persist` under `.{event}-{filename}.{pid}.{seq}.tmp`; a failed write or persist leaves the target untouched and removes the temp.
requirements.limits: No fsync policy; concurrent read-modify-write on one sidecar is still last-writer-wins.

requirements.title: Backstop cycles are non-overlapping and drain-complete
requirements.statement: Each per-root backstop cycle runs to completion before another cycle for that root may start: the scan enqueues every difference observed at scan time and the worker queue drains. A tick that arrives while a cycle runs coalesces into at most one follow-up cycle.
requirements.gate: Scheduler test: a cycle slower than the interval does not overlap itself and leaves exactly one coalesced follow-up; cycle completion is defined by the queue draining.
requirements.implementation: The backstop starts a scan job and awaits the job handle; ticks during the wait set one pending follow-up. Shutdown aborts the loop, rejects new intake, cancels and awaits the active job, then drains the writer; queued intake work is discarded.
requirements.limits: No slow-cycle gate-hold test; completion is observed through the job's terminal state rather than a queue-depth probe.
